name: Section 80C — Investments & Expenses
description: Deduction for investments in PPF, ELSS, EPF, Life Insurance Premium, Home Loan Principal, and School Tuition Fees.

conditions.description: User has reported at least one eligible Section 80C investment or expense.

explanationTemplate: Under Section 80C, you reported a total of ₹{inputValue} in eligible investments. The maximum allowed deduction under the Old Tax Regime is ₹{maximumAllowed}. Your allowed deduction is ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 80D — Medical Insurance & Preventive Checkup
description: Deduction for medical insurance premium paid for self, family, and parents, plus preventive health checkups.

conditions.description: User has reported health insurance premium payments or preventive health checkups.

explanationTemplate: Under Section 80D, health insurance premiums qualify up to ₹25,000 for self/family (₹50,000 if senior citizen) plus up to ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents. You reported ₹{inputValue}, resulting in a deduction of ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 80CCD(1B) — National Pension System (NPS)
description: Additional deduction up to ₹50,000 for voluntary contributions to NPS Tier-I account (over and above 80C).

conditions.description: User has contributed to National Pension System (NPS Tier-I).

explanationTemplate: Section 80CCD(1B) grants an additional tax deduction up to ₹50,000 exclusively for NPS investments. You invested ₹{inputValue}, allowing a deduction of ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 24(b) — Home Loan Interest
description: Deduction for interest paid on home loan for self-occupied house property.

conditions.description: User paid interest on home loan for a residential property.

explanationTemplate: Interest paid on home loan for self-occupied property is deductible up to ₹2,00,000 under Section 24(b). You paid ₹{inputValue}, giving a deduction of ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 80E — Higher Education Loan Interest
description: Deduction for full interest paid on loan taken for higher education of self, spouse, or children (No upper monetary limit).

conditions.description: User paid interest on loan taken for higher education.

explanationTemplate: Under Section 80E, 100% of interest paid on higher education loans is deductible under the Old Tax Regime without an upper monetary limit. You reported ₹{inputValue}, granting full ₹{potentialDeduction} deduction.

name: Section 80EEB — Electric Vehicle (EV) Loan Interest
description: Deduction for interest paid on loan taken for purchasing an Electric Vehicle (EV).

conditions.description: User paid interest on a loan sanctioned for purchasing an Electric Vehicle (EV).

explanationTemplate: Under Section 80EEB, interest paid on electric vehicle (EV) loans is deductible up to ₹1,50,000 under the Old Tax Regime. You reported ₹{inputValue}, granting a deduction of ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Vehicle Expenses & Depreciation (Business / Self-Employed)
description: Tax deduction for vehicle depreciation (15% rate), fuel, maintenance, and driver salary used for business or freelance purposes.

conditions.description: User incurred vehicle fuel, maintenance, or depreciation expenses for business/freelance work.

explanationTemplate: Under Section 32 & 37, vehicle running costs and 15% annual depreciation are valid business deductions for self-employed/freelancers. Reported: ₹{inputValue}, Allowed: ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 80GG — House Rent Paid (No HRA received)
description: Deduction for rent paid by individuals who do not receive House Rent Allowance (HRA) from employer.

conditions.description: User does NOT receive HRA from employer.

explanationTemplate: Under Section 80GG, rent paid (minus 10% income) capped at ₹5,000/month (₹60,000/yr) or 25% total income is deductible when HRA is not provided. Calculated deduction: ₹{potentialDeduction}.

name: Section 80TTA — Interest on Savings Account
description: Deduction up to ₹10,000 on savings account interest for non-senior citizens.

conditions.description: User has earned interest income from savings bank accounts.

explanationTemplate: Section 80TTA allows deduction up to ₹10,000 for savings bank interest for individuals under 60. You reported ₹{inputValue}, yielding ₹{potentialDeduction} deduction.
